identification.doi_note: No DOI covers the ASOS network as a whole. NCEI catalogues its products separately: 1-minute page 1 (DSI 6405, record gov.noaa.ncdc:C00386), 1-minute page 2 with precipitation (DSI 6406, C00387), 5-minute (DSI 6401, C00418) and hourly reports in GHCNh (DSI 2074, C01688). These are NCEI identifiers, not DOIs. A DOI exists only for subsets, such as NCAR/EOL's ASOS 5-minute data for December 2013 to January 2014 (10.26023/RTF3-A0N3-E20P).
identification.project: Automated Surface Observing System (ASOS), a joint NWS, FAA and DoD program
identification.data_provider: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information (NCEI)
identification.description: A U.S. network of automated surface weather stations, mostly at airports, run jointly by the National Weather Service (NWS), the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and the Department of Defense (DoD). It observes precipitation, temperature, wind, pressure, visibility and clouds around the clock. ASOS is a network rather than one fixed-format dataset: its 1-minute, 5-minute, hourly and climatological products have different identifiers and periods of record. NOAA NCEI is the archive of record for all of them.

instruments.summary: Automated accumulation gauges (a heated tipping bucket at most sites, or the newer AWPAG weighing gauge), with freezing-rain and present-weather sensors.

categories.name: Heated Tipping Bucket (HTB)
categories.role: The original ASOS gauge, still at most sites (575 in NWS's March 2025 equipment list, 552 of them FAA): a heated funnel melts frozen precipitation, and each tip records 0.01 inch

categories.name: All Weather Precipitation Accumulation Gauge (AWPAG)
categories.role: Heated weighing gauge for liquid and frozen precipitation that replaced the tipping bucket at NWS-sponsored sites (323 in the March 2025 list); the NWS climate-standard gauge

categories.name: Freezing Rain Sensor (FRS)
categories.role: Detects freezing rain and icing; identifies precipitation rather than measuring amounts

processing_chain: Sensor data collection packages feed the station's Acquisition Control Unit, which applies the algorithms and transmits the reports
Reports travel over NWS or FAA networks to the NWS Telecommunications Gateway and NCEP, then to NCEI
NCEI archives the 1-minute and 5-minute files and the hourly reports (in GHCNh)
instruments.note: Equipment differs from station to station. Snowfall and snow depth are measured by hand, not by ASOS.

temporal.start_note: Start of NCEI's 1-minute record. The 5-minute record starts on 1996-07-01 but has no precipitation amounts, and the hourly reports go back further at some stations. Each station's period of record differs.
temporal.input_frequency: 1-minute gauge accumulations, summed into the hourly, 3-, 6- and 24-hour amounts
temporal.note: Hourly and 1-minute precipitation can cover different accumulation periods and should not be treated as interchangeable.

other_frequencies.availability: Separate NCEI product (DSI 6401); present weather only
Reports issued when conditions change significantly, archived with the hourly reports
Daily Summary Message (DSM) and monthly CF6 summaries; no separate NCEI archive found

spatial.coverage: United States: 50 states, Puerto Rico, U.S. Virgin Islands and some Pacific territories
spatial.note: Stations are mostly at airports. The extent is the 5-minute product's catalog bounding box, not a claim that observations fill it. Use the station coordinates for spatial analysis rather than a grid resolution.

data_format.format: Text (.dat) files by station and month (1-minute, 5-minute); GHCNh files by station and year (hourly)
